Each entry needs: state, county (or null for every county in that state), column, reason (specific, falsifiable), confirmed_date, confidence ('high' = directly verified for this exact cell; 'medium' = inferred from a verified sibling/structural rule, not independently re-checked for every county it covers). gap_matrix.py's roll_up() checks this registry before finalizing each cell's gap_class and overrides to 'declined (<reason>)' when found -- never silently; the override is itself visible in the gap list so a human can challenge it. A declined entry is a claim, not a law: if new evidence contradicts one (the underlying platform adds a field, a law changes, a county switches vendors), remove or correct the entry and re-verify live before trusting the correction.

This project's ROD-platform infrastructure (sc_countyfusion.py, kofile.py, publicsearch.py, etc.) cannot reach Probate Court records at all -- a different county office entirely, not a missing filter. NC tax-foreclosure sales are JUDICIAL (G.S. 105-374 in rem, or power-of-sale under G.S. 45-21.31 for mortgage-style tax foreclosures); any excess-over-debt proceeds are deposited with the CLERK OF SUPERIOR COURT inside that specific foreclosure special-proceeding's own case file, not published by the county tax office as a roster. Claiming requires a motion/petition referencing that case number (G.S. 45-21.31/105-374(q)); there is no county-wide or statewide published list of who has surplus -- confirmed independently two ways: (1) this repo's own gap_matrix.py Spec for this column already carries the ambiguity note 'SC counties publish excess-funds lists; NC clerks hold surplus without a published list', and (2) fresh 2026-11-10 web research (NC probate/estate-law firm Q&A content, a dozen+ independent articles) converges on the same claim-by-petition-to-the-case-file process with no published roster. After ~1 year unclaimed, money can migrate to the NC State Treasurer's generic Unclaimed Property Division (116B-62) -- a DIFFERENT, non-tax-sale-specific statewide database (bank accounts, uncashed checks, etc.), not a fix for this column; scraping it would need heavy filtering and is a separate future signal, not this one. This makes the 101 NC rows the gap matrix flags 'sourced-not-built' for lt_tax_sale_overage a heuristic false-positive (the matrix treats 'county has SOME tax source in county_records_matrix.json' as 'sourced' for every tax-family column, including this one, without checking that source actually publishes an overage list). Verified directly against the structural rule (judicial-foreclosure routing), not independently re-checked clerk-by-clerk for all 100 NC counties -- a county-specific override still wins if one clerk turns out to publish a list anyway.

email has exactly one live producer that is structurally OWNER-sourced: liensnc_handoff.py reads a filed LiensNC lien-agent-designation record (raw.liensnc_related.owner_contact.email / raw.liensnc.owner_text), which exists only because NC Gen. Stat. 44A-11.1/44A-11.2 uniquely requires owners of qualifying NC construction projects to designate a lien agent and record that designation (LiensNC.com is the de facto public registry; confirmed via statute text and vendor commentary, 2026-11-16 web research) -- the OWNER (or their agent) supplies the contact block at filing time, so it genuinely carries the owner, not a third party. South Carolina mechanics-lien law (SC Code Title 29, Chapter 5) has no equivalent lien-agent-designation-with-public-registry mechanism: its closest instruments (29-5-23 Notice of Project Commencement, 29-5-40 Notice to Owner, 29-5-15 contractor licensing proof) are different filings that do not capture an owner email address, and no SC vendor equivalent to LiensNC surfaced in a 2026-11-16 search of SC Title 29 Ch.5 sources. Every OTHER raw e-mail source in this codebase (raw.distressed.agent_email / raw.homeharvest.agent_email -- a listing agent, raw.notice_contact.email -- the filing attorney/trustee from Column legal notices, which IS live and does cover SC) is attorney/agent/broker contact, not the owner, and is correctly excluded from owner_email_of() by design (enrichment_email_extract.py's own stated rule, the 2026-10-09 fix for an escape-artifact/misclassification defect) -- re-wiring notice_contact into this column would reintroduce that defect and would not even serve the outreach use case (a distressed owner cannot be reached by emailing their own foreclosing trustee). SC SOS entity records (sc_sos_entity.py) carry only a registered_agent NAME, never an address or email, so that is not a substitute either. The only remaining path is skip-trace (raw.skip_trace.email_addresses, owner_email_of's final fallback) -- real but gated by per-lookup cost, not a free source. Verified directly for the LiensNC mechanism and the codebase's own email-source inventory (high confidence); the SC-has-no-equivalent-statute claim rests on secondary legal-commentary sources converging on the same reading of SC Title 29 Ch.5, not a certified reading of the current statute text (medium confidence, same bar as the existing SC marriage_license entry).
